sources.note: The Posse Foundation's own nomination-process page (the record's official_source_url): nomination rules, eligibility requirements, nomination timelines, and the full-tuition award statement.
Posse's Recruiting Students hub: describes the annual nomination and Dynamic Assessment Process cycle and the Arts and STEM nomination streams.
Posse's recruitment cities page: traditional and Virtual Programs, Arts and Veterans streams.
Posse Foundation homepage: 'Posse Scholars receive full-tuition leadership scholarships from Posse's partner colleges and universities.'
About Posse: programme components, the September-December Dynamic Assessment Process window, the four-year Campus Program, and college-graduation framing.
Posse's College & University Partners page: partner institutions 'provide Posse Scholars with full-tuition scholarships'.

awarding_body.detail: The page is on possefoundation.org, The Posse Foundation's own domain (its structured data names the organisation 'The Posse Foundation'). The scholarship is Posse's programme: the Foundation recruits, nominates and selects the Scholars, and its partner colleges and universities provide the money. This matches the record's awarding body 'The Posse Foundation'.
awarding_body.quote: The Posse Foundation could not exist without its partner colleges and universities, who provide Posse Scholars with full-tuition scholarships, weekly faculty mentoring, and other support.

deadline.detail: The record carries no deadline (deadline_label null, deadline_precision 'varies') and the page confirms there is no single national deadline: timelines vary by Posse city or programme and applicants are told to contact the local Posse office. The cycle is currently open: the About page states the Dynamic Assessment Process runs September through December each year, so on 12 October 2026 it is under way for fall 2027 entry, and nominations can be made as early as the second semester of junior year.
deadline.quote: Depending on the Posse city or program, nomination timelines and deadlines may vary. Be sure to contact your local Posse office for details at the start of every calendar year.

eligibility.detail: Every distinct claim in the record's eligibility summary is confirmed on the page: nomination by a high school or a community-based organization; being in the first term of the senior year of high school; demonstrated leadership within high school, community or family; demonstrated academic potential; applying on time. The nominator must work with high school juniors/seniors 'in one of Posse's 20-plus recruitment cities', which confirms the record's 'Posse recruitment city' claim. The page adds, consistently, that the Posse Scholarship is neither a minority nor a need-based scholarship. The record's reference to a 'community-based organisation' matches the page's 'community-based organization' (US spelling).
eligibility.quote: To be eligible, a high school senior must: Be nominated by their high school or a community-based organization; Be in the first term of their senior year in high school; Demonstrate leadership within their high school, community or family; Demonstrate academic potential; Apply on time

funding.detail: The award is a full-tuition scholarship at one of Posse's partner colleges or universities, stated word-for-word on the nomination page and the homepage. It is tuition only - living costs, room and board are not covered - so it is correctly recorded as 'Full tuition' rather than 'Fully Funded'. The funds are provided by the partner institutions.
funding.quote: Each Posse Scholar wins a full-tuition scholarship to attend one of Posse's partner colleges or universities.

degree_levels.detail: The pages never print the word 'Bachelor's', but the study level is unambiguous and agrees with the record: eligibility is limited to high school seniors, the award funds study at a partner college or university, the Campus Program is four years, and Posse frames outcomes around graduating from college and first-generation college students. Nothing on the site's recruiting pages offers a graduate-level award.
degree_levels.quote: The four-year Campus Program works to ensure the retention of Posse Scholars and to increase the impact of the program on campus.

recommended_field_updates.deadline_text: Depending on the Posse city or program, nomination timelines and deadlines may vary. Be sure to contact your local Posse office for details at the start of every calendar year. Apply on time; depending on the Posse city or program, nominations are accepted in the spring and summer before senior year begins (contact your local Posse office for specific deadlines).
recommended_field_updates.verification_notes: Verified live on possefoundation.org; the record's official_source_url resolves normally (no redirect wall, no login wall). All record claims confirmed verbatim. Current cycle is open: the Dynamic Assessment Process runs September through December each year, so on 12 Oct 2026 it is running for fall 2027 entry; students may be nominated from the second semester of junior year, and the spring/summer before senior year. Deadline is intentionally not a single date: it varies by Posse city/program and is set by the local Posse office. Watch at next re-check: (1) Posse's own site is internally inconsistent on its footprint (the nomination page says '20-plus recruitment cities' while the Where We Recruit headline now reads '15-plus U.S. cities'), which does not affect this record but may signal a shrinking network; (2) the Posse Arts, Posse STEM and Posse Veterans programs run separate nomination processes and are not covered by this record; (3) the award is full tuition only (provided by the partner colleges) - room, board and other costs are not covered, so the record must not be described as 'Fully Funded'.
